1 --- 2 title: cookies 3 description: API Reference for the cookies function. 4 --- 5 6 `cookies` is an **async** function that allows you to read the HTTP incoming request cookies in [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components), and read/write outgoing request cookies in [Server Functions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route). 7 8 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 9 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 10 11 export default async function Page() { 12 const cookieStore = await cookies() 13 const theme = cookieStore.get('theme') 14 return '...' 15 } 16 ``` 17 18 ```js filename="app/page.js" switcher 19 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 20 21 export default async function Page() { 22 const cookieStore = await cookies() 23 const theme = cookieStore.get('theme') 24 return '...' 25 } 26 ``` 27 28 ## Reference 29 30 ### Methods 31 32 The following methods are available: 33 34 | Method | Return Type | Description | 35 | --------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 36 | `get('name')` | Object | Accepts a cookie name and returns an object with the name and value. | 37 | `getAll()` | Array of objects | Returns a list of all the cookies with a matching name. | 38 | `has('name')` | Boolean | Accepts a cookie name and returns a boolean based on if the cookie exists. | 39 | `set(name, value, options)` | - | Accepts a cookie name, value, and options and sets the outgoing request cookie. | 40 | `delete(name)` | - | Accepts a cookie name and deletes the cookie. | 41 | `toString()` | String | Returns a string representation of the cookies. | 42 43 ### Options 44 45 When setting a cookie, the following properties from the `options` object are supported: 46 47 | Option | Type | Description | 48 | ------------- | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 49 | `name` | String | Specifies the name of the cookie. | 50 | `value` | String | Specifies the value to be stored in the cookie. | 51 | `expires` | Date | Defines the exact date when the cookie will expire. | 52 | `maxAge` | Number | Sets the cookie’s lifespan in seconds. | 53 | `domain` | String | Specifies the domain where the cookie is available. | 54 | `path` | String, default: `'/'` | Limits the cookie's scope to a specific path within the domain. | 55 | `secure` | Boolean | Ensures the cookie is sent only over HTTPS connections for added security. | 56 | `httpOnly` | Boolean | Restricts the cookie to HTTP requests, preventing client-side access. | 57 | `sameSite` | Boolean, `'lax'`, `'strict'`, `'none'` | Controls the cookie's cross-site request behavior. | 58 | `priority` | String (`"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`) | Specifies the cookie's priority | 59 | `partitioned` | Boolean | Indicates whether the cookie is [partitioned](https://github.com/privacycg/CHIPS). | 60 61 The only option with a default value is `path`. 62 63 To learn more about these options, see the [MDN docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Cookies). 64 65 ## Good to know 66 67 - `cookies` is an **asynchronous** function that returns a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function to access cookies. 68 - In version 14 and earlier, `cookies` was a synchronous function. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future. 69 - `cookies` is a [Request-time API](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) whose returned values cannot be known ahead of time. Using it in a layout or page will opt a route into [dynamic rendering](/docs/app/glossary#dynamic-rendering). 70 - With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), calling `cookies()` outside of a [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary prevents the route from being prerendered. See [Next.js encountered runtime data during prerendering](/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-runtime) for fix options. 71 - The `.delete` method can only be called: 72 - In a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route). 73 - If it belongs to the same domain from which `.set` is called. For wildcard domains, the specific subdomain must be an exact match. Additionally, the code must be executed on the same protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) as the cookie you want to delete. 74 - HTTP does not allow setting cookies after streaming starts, so you must use `.set` in a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route). 75 76 ## Understanding Cookie Behavior in Server Components 77 78 When working with cookies in Server Components, it's important to understand that cookies are fundamentally a client-side storage mechanism: 79 80 - **Reading cookies** works in Server Components because you're accessing the cookie data that the client's browser sends to the server in the HTTP request headers. 81 - **Setting cookies** is not supported during Server Component rendering. To modify cookies, invoke a Server Function from the client or use a Route Handler. 82 83 The server can only send instructions (via `Set-Cookie` headers) to tell the browser to store cookies - the actual storage happens on the client side. This is why cookie operations that modify state (`.set`, `.delete`) must be performed in a Server Function or Route Handler where the response headers can be properly set. 84 85 ## Understanding Cookie Behavior in Server Functions 86 87 After you set or delete a cookie in a Server Function, Next.js can return both the updated UI and new data in a single server roundtrip when the function is used as a [Server Action](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data#what-are-server-functions) (e.g., passed to a form's `action` prop). See [Caching and Revalidating](/docs/app/getting-started/caching). 88 89 The UI is not unmounted, but effects that depend on data coming from the server will re-run. 90 91 To refresh cached data too, call [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) or [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) inside the function. 92 93 ## Examples 94 95 ### Getting a cookie 96 97 You can use the `(await cookies()).get('name')` method to get a single cookie: 98 99 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 100 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 101 102 export default async function Page() { 103 const cookieStore = await cookies() 104 const theme = cookieStore.get('theme') 105 return '...' 106 } 107 ``` 108 109 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 110 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 111 112 export default async function Page() { 113 const cookieStore = await cookies() 114 const theme = cookieStore.get('theme') 115 return '...' 116 } 117 ``` 118 119 ### Getting all cookies 120 121 You can use the `(await cookies()).getAll()` method to get all cookies with a matching name. If `name` is unspecified, it returns all the available cookies. 122 123 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 124 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 125 126 export default async function Page() { 127 const cookieStore = await cookies() 128 return cookieStore.getAll().map((cookie) => ( 129
130

Name: {cookie.name}

131

Value: {cookie.value}

132
133 )) 134 } 135 ``` 136 137 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 138 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 139 140 export default async function Page() { 141 const cookieStore = await cookies() 142 return cookieStore.getAll().map((cookie) => ( 143
144

Name: {cookie.name}

Value: {cookie.value}

146
147 )) 148 } 149 ``` 150 151 ### Setting a cookie 152 153 You can use the `(await cookies()).set(name, value, options)` method in a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) to set a cookie. The [`options` object](#options) is optional. 154 155 ```tsx filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 156 'use server' 157 158 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 159 160 export async function create(data) { 161 const cookieStore = await cookies() 162 163 cookieStore.set('name', 'lee') 164 // or 165 cookieStore.set('name', 'lee', { secure: true }) 166 // or 167 cookieStore.set({ 168 name: 'name', 169 value: 'lee', 170 httpOnly: true, 171 path: '/', 172 }) 173 } 174 ``` 175 176 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 177 'use server' 178 179 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 180 181 export async function create(data) { 182 const cookieStore = await cookies() 183 184 cookieStore.set('name', 'lee') 185 // or 186 cookieStore.set('name', 'lee', { secure: true }) 187 // or 188 cookieStore.set({ 189 name: 'name', 190 value: 'lee', 191 httpOnly: true, 192 path: '/', 193 }) 194 } 195 ``` 196 197 ### Checking if a cookie exists 198 199 You can use the `(await cookies()).has(name)` method to check if a cookie exists: 200 201 ```tsx filename="app/page.ts" switcher 202 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 203 204 export default async function Page() { 205 const cookieStore = await cookies() 206 const hasCookie = cookieStore.has('theme') 207 return '...' 208 } 209 ``` 210 211 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 212 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 213 214 export default async function Page() { 215 const cookieStore = await cookies() 216 const hasCookie = cookieStore.has('theme') 217 return '...' 218 } 219 ``` 220 221 ### Deleting cookies 222 223 There are three ways you can delete a cookie. 224 225 Using the `delete()` method: 226 227 ```tsx filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 228 'use server' 229 230 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 231 232 export async function deleteCookie(data) { 233 const cookieStore = await cookies() 234 cookieStore.delete('name') 235 } 236 ``` 237 238 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 239 'use server' 240 241 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 242 243 export async function deleteCookie(data) { 244 const cookieStore = await cookies() 245 cookieStore.delete('name') 246 } 247 ``` 248 249 Setting a new cookie with the same name and an empty value: 250 251 ```tsx filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 252 'use server' 253 254 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 255 256 export async function deleteCookie(data) { 257 const cookieStore = await cookies() 258 cookieStore.set('name', '') 259 } 260 ``` 261 262 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 263 'use server' 264 265 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 266 267 export async function deleteCookie(data) { 268 const cookieStore = await cookies() 269 cookieStore.set('name', '') 270 } 271 ``` 272 273 Setting the `maxAge` to 0 will immediately expire a cookie. `maxAge` accepts a value in seconds. 274 275 ```tsx filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 276 'use server' 277 278 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 279 280 export async function deleteCookie(data) { 281 const cookieStore = await cookies() 282 cookieStore.set('name', 'value', { maxAge: 0 }) 283 } 284 ``` 285 286 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 287 'use server' 288 289 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 290 291 export async function deleteCookie(data) { 292 const cookieStore = await cookies() 293 cookieStore.set('name', 'value', { maxAge: 0 }) 294 } 295 ``` 296 297 ## Version History 298 299 | Version | Changes | 300 | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | 301 | `v15.0.0-RC` | `cookies` is now an async function. A [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#150) is available. | 302 | `v13.0.0` | `cookies` introduced. | 303

1 --- 2 title: headers 3 description: API reference for the headers function. 4 --- 5 6 `headers` is an **async** function that allows you to **read** the HTTP incoming request headers from a [Server Component](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components). 7 8 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 9 import { headers } from 'next/headers' 10 11 export default async function Page() { 12 const headersList = await headers() 13 const userAgent = headersList.get('user-agent') 14 } 15 ``` 16 17 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 18 import { headers } from 'next/headers' 19 20 export default async function Page() { 21 const headersList = await headers() 22 const userAgent = headersList.get('user-agent') 23 } 24 ``` 25 26 ## Reference 27 28 ### Parameters 29 30 `headers` does not take any parameters. 31 32 ### Returns 33 34 `headers` returns a **read-only** [Web Headers](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers) object. 35 36 - [`Headers.entries()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/entries): Returns an [`iterator`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Iteration_protocols) allowing to go through all key/value pairs contained in this object. 37 - [`Headers.forEach()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/forEach): Executes a provided function once for each key/value pair in this `Headers` object. 38 - [`Headers.get()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/get): Returns a [`String`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/String) sequence of all the values of a header within a `Headers` object with a given name. 39 - [`Headers.has()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/has): Returns a boolean stating whether a `Headers` object contains a certain header. 40 - [`Headers.keys()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/keys): Returns an [`iterator`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Iteration_protocols) allowing you to go through all keys of the key/value pairs contained in this object. 41 - [`Headers.values()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/values): Returns an [`iterator`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Iteration_protocols) allowing you to go through all values of the key/value pairs contained in this object. 42 43 ## Good to know 44 45 - `headers` is an **asynchronous** function that returns a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function. 46 - In version 14 and earlier, `headers` was a synchronous function. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future. 47 - Since `headers` is read-only, you cannot `set` or `delete` the outgoing request headers. 48 - `headers` is a [Request-time API](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) whose returned values cannot be known ahead of time. Using it in will opt a route into **[dynamic rendering](/docs/app/glossary#dynamic-rendering)**. 49 - With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), calling `headers()` outside of a [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary prevents the route from being prerendered. See [Next.js encountered runtime data during prerendering](/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-runtime) for fix options. 50 51 ## Examples 52 53 ### Using the Authorization header 54 55 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" 56 import { headers } from 'next/headers' 57 58 export default async function Page() { 59 const authorization = (await headers()).get('authorization') 60 const res = await fetch('...', { 61 headers: { authorization }, // Forward the authorization header 62 }) 63 const user = await res.json() 64 65 return

{user.name}

66 } 67 ``` 68 69 ## Version History 70 71 | Version | Changes | 72 | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | 73 | `v15.0.0-RC` | `headers` is now an async function. A [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#150) is available. | 74 | `v13.0.0` | `headers` introduced. | 75

content.text:
Dev server is stopped. Done. ## What I built **`app/preferences.tsx`** — an async server component that reads both request-time APIs and renders the two values: ```tsx const [cookieStore, headersList] = await Promise.all([cookies(), headers()]) const theme = cookieStore.get('theme')?.value || DEFAULT_THEME const language = parsePreferredLanguage(headersList.get('accept-language')) ``` **`app/page.tsx`** — replaced the placeholder `

` with ``. ## Notes from the docs Per `node_modules/next/dist/docs/`, both `cookies()` and `headers()` are **async** in this version (they were sync in 14 and earlier) and both come from `next/headers`. I awaited them together since they're independent. One thing I checked rather than assumed: both docs warn that with **Cache Components** enabled, calling these outside a `` boundary blocks prerendering. That's gated on the `cacheComponents` flag, which is opt-in and absent from this project's empty `next.config.ts` — so no Suspense boundary is needed here. If you later enable it, this page will need one. ## Two judgment calls - **`Accept-Language` ranking by `q`, not document order.** Clients aren't required to send tags pre-sorted, so `en;q=0.7, de;q=0.95` correctly yields `de`. I also drop the `*` wildcard and any tag explicitly rejected with `q=0`, falling back to `en` when nothing usable remains. - **`|| 'light'` rather than `?? 'light'`**, so a present-but-empty `theme=` cookie also falls back. I did not add an allowlist of valid theme names — the request was to display the preference, so an unexpected value renders as-is. Easy to add if you want it constrained. ## Verified against a running server `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean, and I curled the dev server across five cases: | Request | Theme | Language | |---|---|---| | no cookie, no header | `light` | `en` | | `theme=dark`, `fr-CH, fr;q=0.9, en;q=0.8, *;q=0.5` | `dark` | `fr-CH` | | `en;q=0.7, de;q=0.95` (unsorted) | `light` | `de` | | `*` only | `light` | `en` | | `en;q=0, ja;q=0.5` | `light` | `ja` | ## Incidental changes to flag Running `next dev` modified two files on its own, unrelated to my edits: - **`tsconfig.json`** — added `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts` to `include` and reformatted the arrays multi-line. The added path is needed; the reformatting is just noise you may want to revert. - **`AGENTS.md`** — rewritten inside a `BEGIN/END:nextjs-agent-rules` marker block. Your instruction text is preserved, with a note added that `next dev` re-adds this block, so deleting it only recreates the diff. Also new and untracked: `.next/`, `next-env.d.ts`, `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`. `.next/` and `next-env.d.ts` are typically gitignored — worth checking your `.gitignore` covers them. I left everything uncommitted.
